name: South Park Commons
identity_check: Confirmed as South Park Commons (southparkcommons.com; 380 Brannan St, San Francisco; also written 'SPC'). Ruchi Sanghvi started it in 2016 as a founder community, and about two years later it raised a venture fund and launched the Founder Fellowship. It now runs a six-month Member Residency, a $1M Founder Fellowship and SPC Fund IV ($575M, announced 2026-08-05; Cooley acted as counsel), with hubs in San Francisco, New York and Bengaluru. SPC India is led by GP Prateek Mehta. blog.southparkcommons.com (Substack) is the firm's own blog: its posts are signed by SPC GPs and the main site links it as 'Writing'. Not South Park Ventures, not the South Park (San Francisco) neighbourhood or SouthPark (Charlotte) real-estate entities that turned up in search, and not the TV show.

open_items: Fund IV ($575M) verified, which confirms the lead 'Q3 2026 fund close $575M'. The firm announced it on 2026-08-05 (SPC post, Cooley, Pulse 2.0; AUM about $2B), but no final-close date is published, so the announcement date is used. Wikipedia cites a Bloomberg piece (2026-01-29) saying SPC was planning a $500M fund; Bloomberg was not fetched.

Fund I and II legal names, exact close dates and any upsizing are unverified. SEC EDGAR refused the declared User-Agent, so no Form D was checked, and Forbes (2018) returned 403. Fund II ($150M, 2020) rests on Entrackr plus SPC's press page summary of a 2021 TechCrunch profile (Yahoo syndication was unreachable).

SPC India fund: TechCrunch (Jan 2025) reported an SEC listing targeting $40M; no close or final size was found. The India page shows '$575M Fund', '25 Portfolio Companies' and '150+ Members' as stat blocks. It is unclear whether these are India-only or firm-wide, so portfolio_count_reported is not recorded. The companies page says only 'hundreds of companies'.

invests_in_indian_founders = yes: SPC runs a Bengaluru hub and a 'Founder Fellowship in Bengaluru', GP Prateek Mehta 'leads SPC's India office and investments', and the India portfolio includes Moneyview, Meesho, Arctus Aerospace, Zango AI, Maya Research and QOSMIC. No India-specific terms (INR checks, Indian-entity SAFEs) are published.
requires_us_entity: not stated anywhere. The FAQ says SPC 'cannot directly sponsor visas', and members must work from SF, NYC or Bangalore. Whether India deals need a US flip is unknown.

Fall 2026 Fellowship applications are closed. Spring 2027 is to open 'later this year', and the /apply form also has a rolling 'Funding' pathway for founders already raising. A separate experiment (blog, 2026-10-14) offers '$200k on an uncapped SAFE' via minusone.com, explicitly 'not a formal program'.

Rounds not recorded: Noble Machines (general-purpose industrial robots, Sunnyvale; SPC portfolio, but no disclosed round amount or investors on any fetched page). Arctus Aerospace (Bengaluru high-altitude UAVs; no round page). Cognition Series E, Profound Series D, Baseten Series F, Town Series A, Recursive $650M and Vori Series B appear in SPC monthly updates, but the fetched pages do not state that SPC took part in those specific rounds. Muon Space's Series C release does not name SPC.

Deep Cogito's Business Wire release (2026-08-26) returned 403 and the Economic Times QOSMIC article was unreachable; those rounds rest on SPC's own pages plus SpaceNews/Evertiq for QOSMIC. Lambda Surgical: MDO says 'led by Long Journey Ventures and South Park Commons', and SPC says it co-led, so both are recorded as leads.

Post dates on southparkcommons.com/news are unreliable for older deals: the Baseten post shows June 22, 2026 although Baseten is a long-held company, apparently from a site relaunch. Round dates therefore come from company releases, press or SPC monthly blog updates; post dates are used only for 2026 rounds that the monthly updates confirm.

Jonathan Brebner signed the Nuance Labs post and is listed among the Fellowship's investors, but he has no team page (/team/jonathan returns nothing) and his title is unknown, so he is not recorded. Other investors on the team page (Gopal Raman, Annabelle Pundaky, Rohan Choudhary, Harshit Madan, Tushar Garg) are not recorded: none has a stated AI, industrial or hardware focus.

Partner focus_sectors are classified from the investment posts each partner signed: Agarwal (Deep Cogito, Preseen, Longshot, Rivo), Jacobstein (TenX Semi, Nirva), Itzikowitz (Lambda Surgical, Asymptote). The firm assigns no sector coverage and says the Fellowship is not limited to specific industries.

HQ country and founding year are not stated for several round companies (Asymptote, Deep Cogito, Rivo, Preseen, Nirva, Longshot Space, Goodfire). No website was found on a fetched page for Asymptote (GitHub only), Longshot Space or QOSMIC.
